entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Filippo Pigafetta (1533–1604) was a Venetian mathematician and explorer who played a crucial role in the early modern era of global navigation.

Pigafetta was born in Venice, Italy, around 1533 and served as a mathematician and cartographer for Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan's ill-fated circumnavigation of the globe in 1519–1522. During this voyage, Pigafetta accompanied Magellan to the Philippines, where he documented the region's geography, climate, and native cultures.

Pigafetta's contributions extend beyond his role as a cartographer, however. He was also a skilled mathematician who developed new methods for calculating navigation charts and created detailed maps of the regions they visited. His work on these topics helped pave the way for future explorers and navigators.

Pigafetta returned to Venice in 1522 and continued to work as a mathematician and cartographer, producing several influential works on geography and navigation. Despite his significant contributions to our understanding of the world, Pigafetta's life was cut short when he died on October 26, 1604, at the age of 71.
